item.title: UPDATE: Victims in Rankin County double murder/ suicide identified as local firearms family - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Therese Apel
item.description:
BRANDON — Two people were fatally shot Friday afternoon during a dispute over family land in Rankin County, and the suspected gunman was later found dead of an apparent self-inflicted gunshot wound following a hours-long SWAT standoff, authorities said.

Walter E. Birdsong Jr., 62, and Amanda L. Birdsong, 43, were killed in the shooting on the 1400 block of Monterey Road. The suspected shooter, Kurt Tyler Birdsong, 56, was found dead inside a bathroom of the residence after deputies breached the home, according to the Rankin County Sheriff’s Office.

All three were family members involved in an ongoing dispute over land, investigators said. Deputies responded to a 911 call just before 4 p.m. reporting two people had been shot and that the armed suspect had retreated inside a residence on the property. The Rankin County Sheriff’s Office SWAT Team, negotiators and technical response personnel were among those who responded.

Because the family was involved in a firearms-related business, the sheriff’s office requested assistance from the FBI’s Jackson Field Office, the Mississippi Office of Homeland Security, the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives and the Clinton Bomb Squad, citing an elevated potential threat to law enforcement and nearby residents. Neighbors were evacuated as a precaution.

W.E. Birdsong & Associates Inc., located at 1435 Monterey Road in Florence, has operated since 1973 and holds a federal firearms license issued by the ATF. The company is the manufacturer of Black-T, a proprietary weapons coating used by government and military clients, and is widely regarded in the firearms industry as a leading provider of protective gun finishes.

After armored vehicles arrived, SWAT members and negotiators made multiple attempts to contact the suspect, all of which were unsuccessful. Deputies then used armored and technical equipment to breach the home, where they found Birdsong deceased.

Rankin County Deputy Coroner Cliff Dunlap responded to the scene and transported the deceased.

The investigation is ongoing. The sheriff’s office continues to receive assistance from the FBI and ATF Jackson offices.​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​

item.title: Vehicle strikes Jackson Fire Department building for second time in less than 10 months - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Morgan Howard
item.description:
JACKSON – The Jackson Fire Department said it is making repairs to its Internal Affairs Complex after a vehicle struck the building for the second time in less than 10 months.

The department said the latest incident comes as crews continue working to repair roofs and complete needed upgrades across fire stations.

No staff members working inside the building were injured in the crash, according to the department.

Jackson fire officials said the setbacks have created additional repair needs, but the department remains committed to improving its facilities for firefighters and the community.

The department thanked residents for their patience and support as it works through the unexpected challenges.

According to the Rankin County Sheriff’s Department, the suspect is barricaded inside of a home in the 1400 block of Monterrey Road near Florence.

Sheriff Bryan Bailey said that the two family members who were killed are somehow related to the suspect.

The road is completely blocked. All drivers are being asked to avoid the area and take a detour.

We are live at the scene and will continue to bring you the latest updates.

item.title: State Officials Warn Storm Survivors to Watch for Contractor Fraud During Recovery Efforts - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Therese Apel
item.description:
JACKSON — Mississippi officials are encouraging homeowners affected by recent storms in the southern part of the state to carefully research contractors before agreeing to repair work, citing concerns about fraud and unlicensed construction activity in damaged communities.

The Mississippi State Board of Contractors said periods following severe weather often lead to an increase in questionable repair offers from out-of-town operators and scammers targeting residents eager to rebuild.

“Storm recovery creates urgency, and unfortunately scammers count on that,” Stephanie Lee said in a statement. “We understand families want to rebuild quickly, but rushing into an agreement with an unlicensed contractor can lead to unfinished work, unsafe repairs and significant financial loss.”

The agency said homeowners should verify that contractors are properly licensed before allowing work to begin. Licensed contractors are subject to state oversight and regulatory standards, officials said.

The warning comes as many South Mississippi residents continue cleaning up damage caused by recent storms and severe weather.

According to the Federal Trade Commission, complaints involving home repair scams routinely increase after natural disasters. Officials said warning signs can include contractors going door-to-door, demanding large upfront payments or pressuring residents to sign contracts immediately.

The contractors board recommends that homeowners seek referrals from trusted sources, obtain multiple written estimates and avoid paying the full cost of a project before work is completed. Residents are also urged to insist on written contracts outlining the scope of work, project timeline and payment terms.

Officials said consumers should use traceable forms of payment and report suspicious activity or unlicensed work to the state board.

“Choosing a licensed contractor is one of the most important decisions a homeowner can make after a storm,” Lee said. “Our goal is to help Mississippi families recover safely, responsibly and without becoming victims of fraud during an already difficult time.”

The Mississippi State Board of Contractors regulates the state’s construction industry and investigates complaints involving unlicensed contractors and other violations.

item.title: Purdue-Sackler opioid settlement takes effect, bringing nearly $41M to Mississippi - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Morgan Howard
item.description:
JACKSON – Mississippi is expected to receive nearly $41 million over the next 15 years after a $7.4 billion settlement with Purdue Pharma and the Sackler family became legally effective May 1, Attorney General Lynn Fitch announced.

The settlement caps more than a decade of work by attorneys general across the country over Purdue’s and the Sacklers’ role in the opioid crisis. Mississippi sued Purdue in December 2015, shortly before a multistate investigation was launched.

“The opioid epidemic has claimed far too many lives in Mississippi, leaving behind lasting pain,” Fitch said. “This settlement is another step toward holding accountable those who played a role in this epidemic and toward healing for many Mississippians who lost loved ones. Together, we can address the harm already done and prevent more senseless deaths.”

Purdue filed for bankruptcy in September 2019 amid widespread litigation. Attorneys general have played a lead role in the bankruptcy proceedings.

The settlement resolves litigation against Purdue and the Sackler family for producing and aggressively marketing opioids in the United States. Fifty-five attorneys general representing eligible U.S. states and territories previously signed onto the settlement.

Mississippi is expected to receive $40,958,248.92 from the settlement. Fitch’s office said the latest agreement brings the total amount of opioid settlement funds secured for Mississippi to more than $400 million.

The settlement permanently bars the Sacklers from selling opioids in the United States and provides money for addiction treatment, prevention and recovery programs nationwide.

Under the agreement, Purdue’s manufacturing operations transferred May 1 to Knoa Pharma LLC, which will be overseen by a board of directors with no connection to Purdue. The settlement also prevents Knoa from marketing opioids and requires an independent monitor to ensure the company provides the medicines in a manner intended to limit the risk of diversion.

The settlement also requires Purdue and the Sacklers to make public more than 30 million documents related to their opioid business.

item.title: Monticello animal rescue asks for donations after founder’s property hit by tornado - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Morgan Howard
item.description:
MONTICELLO – Safe Haven Rescue MS is asking for donations after the rescue’s founder and president was directly impacted by a tornado Wednesday evening.

The rescue said its founder’s property was hit by an EF-4/EF-5 tornado. The founder, her dogs and all of the rescue dogs were safe and unharmed, according to the organization.

Safe Haven Rescue MS said one of the biggest losses was the rescue’s transport van, which was crushed after trees fell and were uprooted. The founder also lost her personal truck.

The rescue said replacing the transport van is a major expense and one the organization cannot afford on its own.

Safe Haven Rescue MS said many animals depend on the rescue and asked the public to consider donating or sharing the request with others.

The organization also asked for prayers for those affected by the storm.

You can donate to the rescue on their Facebook page below.

/p>

item.title: Mississippi Supreme Court closes door on juvenile lifer's final appeal - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Therese Apel
item.description:
JACKSON — The Mississippi Supreme Court has refused to hear the final appeal of a man sentenced to life in prison for crimes he committed at age 14, ending his decades-long legal fight for the chance at parole.

The state’s high court rejected David Moody’s petition on May 1, 2026, with six justices voting to deny and one voting to grant. The decision leaves intact a Mississippi Court of Appeals ruling from August 2025 that upheld Moody’s life-without-parole sentence.

Moody, now in his mid-40s, has been incarcerated since 2000 for his role in the 1995 deaths of Robbie Bond and William Hatcher in Perry County. He was 14 years old at the time.

The case had worked its way back through the courts after a 2012 U.S. Supreme Court ruling required judges to individually consider a juvenile’s age, background and potential for rehabilitation before sentencing them to life without parole. A three-day hearing was held in Perry County in February 2024, after which the circuit judge decided the sentence should stand. The Court of Appeals agreed, and now the Mississippi Supreme Court has declined to second-guess that decision.

On the night of May 14, 1995, Moody and his older cousin Kenneth Moody were with the young couple at a bridge in Perry County when Kenneth Moody attacked and killed Hatcher, then kidnapped, raped and murdered Bond. David Moody maintained throughout the proceedings that Kenneth threatened to kill him if he did not cooperate, and DNA evidence supported his claim that he did not rape Bond. He came forward to police four days later and led investigators to the bodies.

The former Forrest County sheriff who first took David Moody’s statement testified at the 2024 hearing that the case was “the biggest injustice and travesty of justice” of his 44-year career.

Courts ultimately pointed to David Moody’s prison disciplinary record of more than 60 violations including possession of homemade weapons, contraband cell phones and threatening a corrections officer in concluding he had not shown the capacity for rehabilitation.

A dissenting judge on the Court of Appeals argued the majority placed too much weight on the severity of the crime and not enough on the reality that Moody was a frightened child under the control of a violent older relative with no way to escape. Two justices on the Supreme Court agreed the case deserved a closer look, but were outvoted.

With the state Supreme Court’s refusal to act, Moody has no remaining avenues for appeal within the Mississippi court system.

item.title: Mississippi Insurance Department urges storm victims to document damage, file claims quickly - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Therese Apel
item.description:
JACKSON — The Mississippi Insurance Department is encouraging homeowners affected by the May 6-7 storms to begin documenting damage and contacting their insurance companies as recovery efforts continue across the state.

State officials said residents should first review their insurance deductibles, assess property damage and determine whether filing a claim is necessary.

The department urged policyholders to begin the claims process as soon as possible, noting that some insurance policies contain deadlines for reporting storm-related damage.

Officials also advised residents to gather policy information before filing claims and keep detailed records of conversations with insurance companies, creditors and relief agencies throughout the recovery process.

The agency recommends taking photographs or video of damaged property and creating an inventory of damaged or missing items before insurance adjusters arrive. Homeowners were also advised to save receipts for temporary repairs and emergency expenses.

According to the department, residents should make only temporary repairs needed to prevent additional damage — such as covering broken windows or leaking roofs — until adjusters inspect the property and repair costs are agreed upon.

Officials said homeowners displaced by storm damage should ask insurers whether their policies include coverage for additional living expenses.

The department also cautioned residents to keep damaged personal property available for inspection and to request itemized explanations of claim settlement offers from adjusters.

State officials noted that smaller claims may be resolved quickly, while widespread storm damage could result in longer processing times for larger claims.

Residents needing assistance with insurance questions or claims can contact the Mississippi Insurance Department by phone or through its website.

item.title: MDWFP to host free Fish Camp for youth in June - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Morgan Howard
item.description:
ENID – The Mississippi Department of Wildlife, Fisheries, and Parks will host a free Fish Camp for youth ages 10 to 15 in June.

The camp will be held from 9 a.m. to 3 p.m. June 10 at the Bob Tyler Fish Hatchery Visitor Education Center.

The full-day camp will include fish identification, water safety tips, a tour of the hatchery and catfish fishing in the Visitor Education Center pond.

Participants will also meet a National Park Service ranger and learn more about the Jr. Angler Badge.

The program is free, but space is limited and preregistration is required.

To preregister, call the Visitor Education Center at 662-563-8068 or email [email protected] to receive a registration form.

item.title: MDWFP Announces Temporary Boat Access Restrictions at Two State Parks for July 4 Events - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Therese Apel
item.description:
JACKSON — The Mississippi Department of Wildlife, Fisheries, and Parks announced temporary boat access restrictions at two state parks during Fourth of July holiday events connected to America 250 celebrations.

At Paul B. Johnson State Park, boat access to the lake will be closed from 8 a.m. to 1 p.m. July 3 while water-based activities and holiday events take place.

At Percy Quin State Park, boat access will be limited throughout the day July 3 and July 4 because of scheduled Independence Day celebrations and activities.

Officials said only overnight guests at Percy Quin State Park will be allowed lake access during the restrictions, and those visitors must coordinate with park staff for designated launch and retrieval times.

The temporary restrictions apply only to boat access. Visitors will still be permitted to fish from the banks of the lakes during closure periods, according to MDWFP.

The agency said the adjustments are intended to help ensure public safety during the holiday weekend festivities.

Additional information about America 250 celebrations at Mississippi state parks is available through MDWFP.

item.title: Man known as "BooBay" charged with murder, given $1M bond in Jackson backyard homicide - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Morgan Howard
item.description:
JACKSON – A Jackson man has been charged with murder after he was arrested Wednesday, police said.

The Jackson Police Department said officers responded at about 8:30 p.m. May 7 to the 1800 block of Chadwick Drive, where they arrested Arius Henderson, 38, also known as “BooBay.”

He was arrested in connection with the shooting that happened yesterday when a man was found shot to death in a backyard on Gaites Lane.

UPDATE: Man found shot to death in South Jackson backyard identified

Police said Henderson was taken to JPD headquarters and interviewed before being booked into city holding.

Henderson appeared before a municipal court judge Thursday morning and was given a combined bond of $1 million. Police said the bond included $900,000 for murder and $100,000 for convicted felon in possession of a firearm.

The investigation is ongoing.

Anyone with information is asked to contact the Jackson Police Department at 601-960-1604 or Crime Stoppers at 601-355-TIPS (8477). Crime Stoppers said tipsters may be eligible for a reward of up to $2,500 if information leads to an arrest.

item.title: Man extradited to George County in sexual, physical abuse case - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Morgan Howard
item.description:
GEORGE COUNTY – A man previously arrested in Alabama after an investigation into multiple reports of sexual and physical abuse has been extradited to George County, according to the George County Sheriff’s Office.

Tony K. Fairley, 49, was previously arrested in Baldwin County, Alabama, after an extensive investigation by George County authorities.

The sheriff’s office said Fairley was initially charged with three counts of sexual battery and two counts of child abuse after multiple people came forward reporting incidents that allegedly happened over several years.

Since Fairley’s return to George County, additional charges of molestation and grooming have been filed, according to the sheriff’s office.

Bond was set at $200,000 each for the three sexual battery charges, $50,000 each for the two child abuse charges, $50,000 for the molestation charge and $50,000 for the grooming charge. The total bond amount is $800,000.

Fairley is being held at the George County Regional Correctional Facility pending further court proceedings.

Sheriff Mitchell Mixon said the case reflects the dedication of investigators and the department’s commitment to protecting victims in George County.

The sheriff’s office said the investigation remains focused on protecting the community and holding offenders accountable.

Fairley is presumed innocent unless and until proven guilty in court.

item.title: Lincoln County deputies to offer meals, supplies at Charity Baptist Church in aftermath of storms - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Morgan Howard
item.description:
LINCOLN COUNTY – The Lincoln County Sheriff’s Office said deputies will be back at Charity Baptist Church to provide food and supplies for residents affected by recent storms.

Deputies said they will be at the church beginning at 9 a.m. with coffee and muffins.

At 11 a.m., burgers, hot dogs and tacos will be served. The sheriff’s office said enough food will be available for 600 people.

Deputies also said the grill will be going throughout the day. Residents who have food in their freezers and do not want it to go to waste are encouraged to bring it by so it can be cooked.

Donations will also be available for residents and families, including diapers, wipes, toilet paper, water, toothbrushes, toothpaste, snacks and canned goods.

The sheriff’s office said residents who are unable to get to the church can reach out, and deputies will work to get supplies to them.

item.title: At least 5 tornadoes carved paths across south Mississippi Wednesday night - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Therese Apel
item.description:
JACKSON — Two powerful EF3 tornadoes were in a group of at least five twisters that tore across South Mississippi during Wednesday night’s severe weather outbreak, leaving behind long paths of destruction, multiple injuries and hundreds of documented damage sites, according to preliminary findings from the National Weather Service office in Jackson.

The strongest storms included the Garden City tornado, which reached peak winds of 136 mph and traveled 30.7 miles, and the East Franklin-to-Monticello tornado, which packed 137 mph winds along a 35.9-mile path stretching more than a half-mile wide at times.

The Franklin-to-Monticello tornado injured 12 people and grew as wide as 2,050 yards, making it one of the most significant storms of the outbreak. The Garden City tornado injured one person and reached a maximum width of 1,600 yards.

Despite the intensity of the storms, officials said no fatalities were reported in any of the five confirmed tornadoes.

National Weather Service survey teams said they assessed more than 70 miles of tornado tracks and documented 472 separate damage points Thursday. Officials said additional survey work remains underway, including areas in Lamar and Forrest counties that had not yet been fully examined as of Thursday night.

The weather service said more analysis will continue in the coming days using drone footage and high-resolution satellite imagery, and additional adjustments to tornado ratings and path details remain possible.

In addition to the two EF3 tornadoes, survey teams confirmed three weaker tornadoes:

Officials described the two EF3 tornadoes as the most destructive storms of the evening, particularly the Franklin-to-Monticello tornado because of its length, width and number of injuries.

item.title: VA appointments may move to telehealth after Mississippi tornadoes - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Morgan Howard
item.description:
JACKSON – The G.V. “Sonny” Montgomery VA Medical Center is urging veterans to avoid travel in areas impacted by severe tornadoes.

The medical center said several communities in the area were affected, including locations near some of its Community-Based Outpatient Clinic sites.

Emergency management officials are urging people to stay off the roads, especially in Lincoln and Franklin counties, so search and rescue teams can operate safely.

VA officials said veterans with scheduled appointments at CBOCs in affected counties should not travel until conditions are safe. The VA said it will work with patients to reschedule appointments or transition them to telehealth visits.

Anyone in immediate danger or in need of emergency medical assistance should call 911.

Veterans in crisis can contact the Veterans Crisis Line 24/7 by calling 988 and pressing 1, texting 838255 or chatting online at VeteransCrisisLine.net.

Veterans who need to cancel, reschedule or request a virtual visit can contact the Clinical Contact Center at 1-800-949-1009 or 601-362-4471. They can also contact the VISN 16 Clinical Contact Center at 1-833-363-1063.

The VA also encouraged veterans to use the VA Health Chat app to connect with VA staff from home.

item.title: Three charged after wire theft complaint leads to police pursuit in Greenville - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Morgan Howard
item.description:
GREENVILLE – Authorities said narcotics investigators were conducting proactive patrol May 7 when they responded to information received through dispatch about people allegedly stealing wire in the Juniper Street area.

While responding, investigators received additional information that a suspicious pickup truck had been seen leaving the area and traveling onto Canal Street.

Investigators said they located a pickup truck matching the description traveling at a high rate of speed on Canal Street. Near the intersection of Canal and Reed streets, investigators said they saw the driver fail to stop at a stop sign while making a left turn.

Authorities activated emergency equipment to attempt a traffic stop, but the driver refused to stop and accelerated, leading to a pursuit, according to investigators.

During the pursuit, the vehicle continued through multiple intersections, disregarded traffic control devices and ran a traffic signal at Reed and Main streets.

Investigators said the vehicle also struck multiple road maintenance cones while attempting to evade law enforcement.

Additional patrol units joined the pursuit, which ended when the vehicle turned onto Wall Street and stopped at the end of the road.

The occupants were detained and identified as Joshua Colyer, 44, of Indianola; Tristen Vanderford, 24, of Hollandale; and Brandi Flemmons, 26, of Leland.

Investigators said they found a large quantity of freshly cut communication wire in the bed of the pickup truck.

All three were charged with grand larceny. Colyer was also charged with multiple traffic-related offenses connected to the pursuit.

The vehicle was impounded as part of the ongoing investigation. During the booking process, investigators said Colyer made an unsolicited statement claiming one of the passengers was only along for the ride and was not involved in the alleged theft.

Authorities said the statement will be reviewed as part of the continuing investigation. All three suspects are presumed innocent unless and until proven guilty in court.

item.title: Storms leave 17 injured, hundreds of homes damaged in Mississippi - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Morgan Howard
item.description:
PEARL – Mississippi officials are continuing to assess damage after severe storms moved through the state overnight, leaving at least 17 people injured, Gov. Tate Reeves said.

READ MORE DETAILED COVERAGE ON THE STORMS HERE.

Reeves said initial damage assessments show 275 homes and 50 apartment units were damaged or inaccessible in Lamar County. Thirty roads were also closed because of debris, and the county shelter and safe room remained open. American Red Cross support was available.

In Lincoln County, more than 200 homes were damaged. Reeves said the Cajun Navy is deploying a 50-person shelter pod, a 30-kilowatt generator and 10 pallets of supplies.

In Lawrence County, 12 homes were damaged, and multiple roads were closed because of downed trees and power lines.

Officials said the numbers are preliminary and are expected to change as damage assessments continue.

The Mississippi Emergency Management Agency is supporting damage and operations assessments. Reeves said road-clearing teams are being deployed to remove debris, and the state is sending additional resources as requested by local emergency managers.

LUCEDALE – A Lucedale man has been charged with aggravated assault after a shooting in George County, according to the George County Sheriff’s Office.

When deputies arrived, they secured the scene and began an investigation.

Investigators with the George County Criminal Investigations Division identified Mason D. McCarty, 29, of Lucedale, as the suspect in the shooting. A warrant was later issued for his arrest.

McCarty is being held at the George County Regional Correctional Facility, where he is awaiting his initial appearance before a George County Justice Court judge.

Sheriff Mitchell Mixon said violence has no place in the community and praised patrol deputies and investigators for quickly identifying and apprehending the suspect.

The sheriff’s office said the case remains under investigation and no additional information will be released at this time.

McCarty is presumed innocent unless and until proven guilty in court.

item.title: Three Jackson firefighters placed on leave after alleged on-duty alcohol violation - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Therese Apel
item.description:
JACKSON — Three Jackson Fire Department firefighters have been placed on administrative leave after officials said they violated departmental policy while on duty over the weekend.

According to a statement released by Mayor John Horhn’s office, the firefighters visited a downtown Jackson establishment during their shift before being dispatched to a fire at a blighted property.

After the fire response, law enforcement officers were called and administered sobriety testing, officials said. The firefighters were found to be in violation of department policy.

Fire Chief Rasean Thomas said he was immediately notified and placed the firefighters on administrative leave pending the outcome of an internal investigation.

“The conduct described in this incident is unacceptable and inconsistent with the standards we demand of every member of this department,” Thomas said in the release. “The safety of Jackson residents is our highest obligation, and any behavior that compromises that obligation will not be tolerated.”

City officials did not release the names of the firefighters involved or specify the exact policy violations.

Horhn said he has directed Thomas to strengthen the department’s alcohol policy and implement stricter enforcement procedures.

“We are taking this matter with the utmost seriousness,” Horhn said. “I have directed Chief Thomas to strengthen the department’s alcohol policy and institute more rigorous enforcement procedures to ensure an incident of this nature does not occur again.”

In a department-wide memo dated May 4, Thomas told employees there would be “zero tolerance” for alcohol or drug use on station premises or while on duty. The memo states violations will result in swift disciplinary action.

item.title: Mississippi proposes updates to park fees, fishing limits and hunting regulations - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Therese Apel
item.description:
JACKSON — The Mississippi Department of Wildlife, Fisheries and Parks is proposing a series of changes to park fees, fishing and boating permits, and hunting regulations, with public comment now open for the next 30 days.

The proposed updates were presented during the April meeting of the Mississippi Commission on Wildlife, Fisheries and Parks and would affect state parks, fisheries and wildlife management rules statewide.

Among the proposed park changes are adjustments to age ranges for annual permits and boat launch fees, adding ages 16 and older to daily fishing fees and lowering the senior age classification from 65 to 62. The department also plans to rename “fishing permits” as “boating permits” to better align with current regulations.

Fisheries proposals include updated crappie limits at Lake Mary Crawford, Simpson County Lake and Horseshoe Lake, as well as revised largemouth bass regulations at several public fishing lakes. Officials also proposed changes to bream limits at Simpson County Lake and a no-harvest rule for walleye at Elvis Presley Lake.

Commercial fishing regulations could also change, including reducing mesh size requirements for hoop nets and prohibiting the possession or transport of live catfish measuring 34 inches or larger.

Wildlife officials are proposing new restrictions for turkey hunting, including reducing the nonresident seasonal bag limit from three birds to two. Nonresident hunters would be limited to one bird before April 1, and all hunters would be restricted to one bird during Wildlife Management Area draw hunts.

According to the department, the proposed changes reflect input from anglers and hunters and aim to align Mississippi’s rules with those in neighboring states while maintaining sustainable wildlife populations.

The proposals are available for public review and comment for 30 days on the department’s website.

The Mississippi Department of Wildlife, Fisheries and Parks said its mission is to conserve and enhance the state’s natural resources while providing quality outdoor recreation opportunities.

item.title: Mississippi appeals court revives wrongful death lawsuit over 2021 death of Damien Cameron - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Therese Apel
item.description:
JACKSON — A Mississippi appeals court has revived a wrongful death lawsuit against two Rankin County sheriff’s deputies and the county itself, ruling Monday that disputed facts about how deputies restrained Damien Cameron before his July 2021 death must be decided by a jury.

The Mississippi Court of Appeals voted 7-3 to reverse the summary judgment in favor of Deputies Hunter Elward and Luke Stickman, finding factual disputes about whether their use of force was excessive and whether they were entitled to qualified immunity. The court also reversed summary judgment for Rankin County on state law claims. The decision was issued May 5.

Cameron, who was known as “Toot,” died after deputies arrested him at his home on Foote Drive in Braxton following a vandalism complaint at a neighbor’s house. A toxicology report later found methamphetamine in his system. The state medical examiner listed the cause and manner of death as “undetermined.”

Cameron’s mother, Monica Lee, sued Rankin County, Elward and Stickman, alleging the deputies used excessive force in violation of the Fourth Amendment and state law under the Mississippi Tort Claims Act.

At the center of the dispute is what happened after Stickman arrived to help Elward handcuff Cameron. Lee and her parents told Mississippi Bureau of Investigation agents that Stickman knelt on Cameron’s neck as he lay prone on the floor, and that Cameron repeatedly said he could not breathe. Stickman said in his report that he knelt beside Cameron with minimal pressure on his back.

The plaintiffs’ expert, Dr. Shandelle Norford, concluded to a reasonable degree of medical probability that Cameron died of cardiopulmonary arrest caused by neck and back compression from both officers during restraint, which she termed “restraint associated asphyxia” with methamphetamine as a contributing factor.

Writing for the majority, Chief Judge Virginia Carlton Barnes said those conflicting accounts created questions of fact that a circuit court cannot resolve at summary judgment.

“Taking into account the consistent testimony by Lee and her parents that Damien repeatedly told the deputies that ‘he couldn’t breathe’ after both deputies subdued him by using their body weight to kneel on his back and neck, we find there was a genuine issue of fact whether these actions constituted a prohibited ‘choke hold’ under the County’s policies and procedures and were excessive force in violation of the Fourth Amendment,” Barnes wrote.

The Rankin County Sheriff’s Department’s own use-of-force policy expressly prohibits choke holds, defined to include applying pressure to a person’s neck. Sheriff Bryan Bailey acknowledged in a deposition that if a deputy applied force to Cameron’s neck with a knee, it would have violated that policy.

The majority also pointed to Elward’s subsequent criminal conviction for falsifying incident reports as a factor bearing on his credibility, and cited a Fifth Circuit ruling that it is a question of fact for a jury to determine whether a person who appeared to be resisting was “merely trying to get into a position where he could breathe.”

The court additionally found a factual dispute over a third use of a Taser, this time in drive-stun mode on Cameron’s thigh after he had already been handcuffed and placed partially in a patrol car, noting Cameron had been tased twice before and had been asserting that he could not breathe.

In a partial dissent joined by Judge John Emfinger and in part by Presiding Judge Jack Wilson, Judge Lassitter St. Pé argued the circuit court reached the right result and should have been affirmed. She wrote that the undisputed evidence showed Cameron actively resisted throughout the encounter and that the deputies ceased using force once he was restrained.

“By reversing that decision, the majority substitutes speculation for evidence and weakens the protections afforded by both qualified immunity and the summary judgment framework,” Lassitter St. Pé wrote.

The appeals court unanimously upheld the circuit court’s denial of Lee’s motion to file a second amended complaint, which sought to add Monell claims and supervisory liability allegations against Rankin County. The court found the motion was filed three weeks past the scheduling order’s deadline and would have caused undue prejudice to the defendants.

The case now returns to Rankin County Circuit Court. The excessive force claim against the individual deputies will be decided by a jury; the state law claim against Rankin County under the Mississippi Tort Claims Act will be decided by the trial judge.

item.title: Man denied bond after two wounded in Jackson shooting, police say - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Therese Apel
item.description:
JACKSON — A 23-year-old man has been charged after two people were wounded in a shooting Tuesday night at an apartment complex on Shaw Road, according to the Jackson Police Department.

Police said officers responded around 9:22 p.m. to the 5000 block of Shaw Road in reference to an aggravated assault.

When officers arrived, they found a red Dodge Challenger that had been struck by gunfire. Investigators said the vehicle was occupied by a 24-year-old man and an 18-year-old man, both of whom suffered gunshot wounds while inside the car.

According to police, the victims told officers they were entering the complex gate when a man later identified as Synterrius Williams fired into the passenger side of the vehicle. Authorities said neither victim knew Williams.

Both victims were transported by ambulance to a local hospital.

Police later apprehended Williams at Building 2 of the complex. Detectives with the department’s Robbery/Homicide Division, hostage negotiators and Mobile Crime personnel assisted at the scene.

Williams was charged with shooting into an occupied vehicle and two counts of aggravated assault. Police said he appeared in municipal court Wednesday and was denied bond.

Officials said FEMA staff always carry official photo identification, and residents should confirm they are speaking with an agency employee before providing any information.

FEMA said it works with the Department of Homeland Security and the U.S. Department of Justice to protect disaster assistance and investigate fraud.

Anyone who suspects fraud can call the Disaster Fraud Hotline at 866-720-5721 or visit fema.gov/disaster-fraud.

item.title: Dr. Jelani C. Zarif inspires JSU graduates to see degrees as pathways to leadership - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Special to Darkhorse Press
item.description:
By Anthony Howard and Jatavian Walker Jackson State University

JACKSON — Jackson State University honored its Spring 2026 graduate class during commencement exercises at the Lee E. Williams Athletics and Assembly Center, celebrating students whose academic journeys reflected perseverance, global scholarship and personal triumph.

JSU’s 14th president, Denise Jones Gregory, Ph.D., presided over her first commencement ceremony since being named in April. She said the Spring 2026 graduating class reflects the university’s mission of academic excellence, leadership development and student success, noting that the graduates continue to demonstrate resilience and readiness to serve communities locally and globally.

“Jackson State University is proud to celebrate the Class of 2026 and all they have accomplished to reach this moment,” said Gregory. “Commencement is a special time on our campus. It marks the work our students have put in and the people who supported them along the way. We are grateful to everyone who helped make this moment possible and look forward to recognizing our graduates as they step into this next chapter.”

The ceremony featured keynote remarks from Dr. Jelani C. Zarif at the Jackson State University Spring 2026 Graduate Commencement Ceremony, who encouraged graduates to embrace resilience, purpose and long-term growth.

“It’s not necessarily a sprint; it’s a journey—and the journey is worth it,” said Zarif, an award-winning researcher who holds the Robert E. Meyerhoff endowed professorship at the Johns Hopkins University School of Medicine, Sidney Kimmel Comprehensive Cancer Center. He urged graduates to reframe challenges as preparation for leadership and impact.

“There will be moments when the path feels uncertain,” he said, emphasizing that success is built through sustained effort and perseverance. “But those moments are not meant to break you—they are meant to build you.”

Zarif also challenged graduates to view their degrees as a call to service. “Your degree is not just a personal achievement— it is a responsibility to serve, to lead and to uplift others.”

Among the graduates was Tameka J. Battle from Jackson, Mississippi, who earned an Education Specialist degree in K–12 Administration and Supervision while overcoming a breast cancer diagnosis.

Battle said she continued her academic work throughout treatment with support from JSU faculty and staff. “This degree was very hard for me,” she said. “While within the program here at Jackson State, I was diagnosed with breast cancer.”

She added that perseverance and support carried her through the program. “My professors and my department chair… worked with me as far as getting my courses done,” she said. “But God gave me the strength and the power to accomplish this goal.”

Battle shared that she was diagnosed as cancer-free in February 2026.

The ceremony also recognized Edna Carolyn Frazier McCallum, a member of JSU’s “Golden Class,” who returned to campus decades after first earning her degrees in music and education.

McCallum reflected on her longstanding connection to the university. “I loved every minute of Jackson State,” she said. “I just loved the music industry.”

She noted the significance of returning alongside family generations connected to JSU. “I’m so proud that she followed in my footsteps,” she said, referencing her granddaughter, a 2023 JSU graduate.

Graduate Shadrack Barffour Awuah from Ghana earned a master’s degree in Public Health after completing undergraduate medical studies in Ukraine. He said JSU’s research focus drew him to the university.

“I love Public Health,” Awuah said. “Reading through how they are very active in research was the main reason why it led me to come here [Jackson State].”

Southern New Jersey native and doctoral graduate Armando Rijo earned a Ph.D. in Urban Higher Education. He credited JSU’s cohort model and academic community for supporting his success.

“It was a great experience,” Rijo said. “They really held me down and kept me moving throughout the entire program.”

CARROLL COUNTY — A 22-year-old man was arrested after deputies executed a search warrant at a residence in the McCarley area, authorities said.

Deputies with the Carroll County Sheriff’s Office carried out the warrant Friday, May 1, and reported finding a large amount of marijuana, U.S. currency and digital scales during the investigation.

Brandon Joseph Watt was taken into custody and charged with possession of a controlled substance with intent to sell, officials said.

Watt was booked into the Carroll County Regional Correctional Facility, where bond was set at $25,000. He was released on bond Monday.

Sheriff Clint Walker credited deputies for their work on the case and said efforts to combat illegal drugs will continue.

“Illegal drugs promote gun violence, as well as property crimes, and impaired driving,” Walker said. “We will continue to work tirelessly to stop the flow of illegal drugs in our county.”

“Illegal drugs promote gun violence, as well as property crimes, and impaired driving,” Walker said. “We will continue to work tirelessly to stop the flow of illegal drugs in our county.”
